editorial:
Imagine waking up to find your boss dead and the police thinking you did it. That is exactly what happens to the housekeeper in this gripping story. You will follow a lawyer who takes on the case, but everything changes when he finds out the only person who saw the murder is a teenage girl with autism. She does not talk or act like other witnesses, which makes the whole trial feel like a giant puzzle. The vibe is a mix of a tense courtroom battle and a heartwarming story about friendship and trust. 

You will really love the acting here because the bond between the lawyer and the girl feels very real and sweet. The way the plot unfolds is smart, and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. While some parts feel a bit slow, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you enjoy mysteries that pull at your heartstrings, you should definitely give this a try. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you want the best picture quality, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: In the end, the lawyer helps the girl find her voice in court. She finally testifies and reveals that the real killer was not the housekeeper, but the dead man's own son. The son had killed his father over money and tried to frame the helper. Once the truth comes out, the housekeeper is set free. The movie wraps up with a touching moment showing how the girl has grown more confident thanks to the lawyer's kindness.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves courtroom dramas and stories about unlikely friendships.
